report_name: Attackers Exploit Enterprise Collaboration Tools for Phishing & Malware

threat_actors.name: APT29
threat_actors.description: Observed using compromised Microsoft Teams accounts to send messages impersonating IT support, which contained links to credential harvesting pages.

threat_actors.name: Collaboration Platform Abusers
threat_actors.description: A general classification for threat actors who exploit enterprise collaboration platforms like Microsoft Teams and Slack for malicious activities, including phishing, credential theft, and malware delivery. This activity is characterized by the abuse of trust in authenticated communication channels.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors, including APT29, used identity phishing through compromised Microsoft Teams accounts to send messages with links to credential harvesting pages.

attack_patterns.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
attack_patterns.description: Attackers created their own Slack workspaces to impersonate administrators and employees, sending phishing links that redirect victims to adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing proxies to capture credentials and MFA tokens.

attack_patterns.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: Malicious files, such as .rar archives containing malware, were sent directly to victims via chat platforms like Microsoft Teams and Slack.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution
attack_patterns.description: Attacks relied on the user to execute a malicious payload, for example by opening a malicious .rar file received in a chat message.

attack_patterns.name: DLL Side-Loading
attack_patterns.description: A legitimate application (WinRAR.exe) was used to load a malicious lpk.dll extracted from a .rar archive, a form of DLL side-loading.

attack_patterns.name: Masquerading
attack_patterns.description: Attackers masqueraded their malicious activity as legitimate collaboration by operating from compromised accounts or impersonating trusted entities like IT support.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: Collaboration tools like Teams.exe were observed launching powershell.exe, indicating potential malicious script execution for follow-on actions.

malware.name: lpk.dll
malware.description: A malicious DLL named lpk.dll delivered via a .rar archive in a chat message. It is loaded by a legitimate application like WinRAR.exe through DLL side-loading to execute malicious code.

tools.name: Microsoft Teams
tools.description: Abused as a trusted communication channel to deliver phishing links and malicious files by threat actors.

tools.name: Slack
tools.description: Abused as a trusted communication channel. Attackers created their own workspaces to impersonate employees and send phishing links to AitM proxies.

tools.name: WinRAR
tools.description: Legitimate archive utility used to inadvertently load a malicious lpk.dll via DLL side-loading when a user opens a malicious .rar archive.

infrastructure.name: Credential Harvesting Site
infrastructure.description: Phishing pages linked from malicious messages sent via collaboration tools to steal user credentials.

infrastructure.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Proxy
infrastructure.description: Phishing proxies used to intercept credentials and MFA tokens from victims who were redirected from malicious links sent via Slack.

indicators.name: Malicious Side-Loading DLL lpk.dll File Creation
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Malicious Side-Loading DLL lpk.dll File Creation
id: 9c5b1a3d-8f7e-4b1c-9d5a-6f8b3a2c1d0e
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a file named lpk.dll, which is commonly used in DLL side-loading attacks, as observed in campaigns abusing collaboration tools.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/communication-channel-identity-risks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\lpk.dll'
  filter:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\csrss.exe'
      - '\winlogon.exe'
      - '\wininit.exe'
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects the creation of lpk.dll, a common name for a malicious library used in DLL side-loading attacks.

indicators.name: Collaboration Tool Spawning Archive Utility
indicators.pattern:
title: Collaboration Tool Spawning Archive Utility
id: 1e8d4c6a-0b3c-4e9a-8b1d-9c0a2f8b4d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects a collaboration tool like Microsoft Teams or Slack spawning an archive utility. This may indicate a user opening a malicious archive delivered via chat.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/communication-channel-identity-risks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1204
  - attack.t1105
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Teams.exe'
      - '\slack.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\WinRAR.exe'
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\WinZip.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects a process creation event where a collaboration tool (Teams, Slack) is the parent of an archive utility (WinRAR, 7z), which can indicate a user opening a malicious file from a chat.

indicators.name: Collaboration Tool Spawning Script Interpreter
indicators.pattern:
title: Collaboration Tool Spawning Script Interpreter
id: f5a2b1c0-3d4e-4f5a-6b7c-8d9e0f1a2b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects a collaboration tool like Microsoft Teams or Slack spawning a script interpreter, which is highly suspicious and could indicate code execution from a malicious file or link.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/communication-channel-identity-risks/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1059
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\Teams.exe'
      - '\slack.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects a process creation event where a collaboration tool (Teams, Slack) is the parent of a command-line interpreter, a strong indicator of malicious execution.
